The National Medical Commission (NMC) has proposed changes to the licensing requirements for Foreign Medical Graduates (FMGs) seeking to practise medicine in India. The draft National Medical Commission (Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026, seeks to simplify one of the existing eligibility conditions by changing the requirement related to registration and licensing in the country where the medical degree is awarded.

Under the proposed amendment, foreign medical graduates would only need to be registered with the respective professional regulatory body in the country where they obtained their medical degree. The draft removes the existing requirement that candidates must hold, or be eligible for, a licence to practise medicine equivalent to that granted to citizens of the country concerned.

Advt

NMC invites objections and suggestions on draft amendmentThe proposed amendment seeks to modify sub-clause (b) of Clause 4 of the National Medical Commission (Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate) Regulations, 2021, originally notified on November 18, 2021.The NMC has invited objections and suggestions from affected stakeholders and members of the public. The draft will be considered after 30 days from the date on which copies of the Gazette notification are made available to the public.

Suggestions must be submitted by email to ug.fmgl.amend2026@nmc.org.in, addressed to the Deputy Secretary (UGMEB), National Medical Commission. The Commission has specified that submissions sent through physical or other modes will not be entertained.

The draft regulations will come into force from the date of their publication in the Official Gazette, subject to the prescribed regulatory process.

The proposed change does not automatically grant FMGs permission to practise in India. Other applicable eligibility, screening, internship and registration requirements will continue to apply.DGHS approves stipend parity for FMG interns at five institutionsIn a separate development, the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), under the Union Health Ministry, has approved stipend parity for Foreign Medical Graduate interns with Indian Medical Graduate interns at five government medical institutions.

Advt

According to a DGHS communication dated November 16, 2026, the approval covers the following institutions:• Vardhman Mahavir Medical College and Safdarjung Hospital, New Delhi.• Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Medical Sciences and Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, New Delhi.• Lady Hardinge Medical College and Associated Hospitals, New Delhi.• North Eastern Indira Gandhi Regional Institute of Health and Medical Sciences, Shillong.• Regional Institute of Medical Sciences, Imphal.Stipend decision limited to five named institutionsThe approval follows an earlier DGHS order dated August 7, 2026, and refers to the NMC's 2022 circular and the Compulsory Rotating Medical Internship Regulations, 2021.

Advt

The latest communication specifically covers the five named institutions. It does not establish stipend parity across all government and private medical colleges. Decisions regarding FMG intern stipends at other institutions will depend on the respective state and institutional authorities.
